subject: Cognitive Science
title: Hot and Cold States
description: Learn Hot and Cold States in one minute.

hook.text: You swear you'll eat healthy—then see a chocolate cake. In a cold state, you made a hot-state decision.

buildup.text: Loewenstein showed that we systematically fail to predict how emotions will change our future choices.

discovery.text: In a cold (calm) state, you underestimate how hunger, anger, or desire will hijack your plans.

twist.text: In a hot (emotional) state, you can't imagine ever feeling calm again. Each state is blind to the other.

climax.text: This 'empathy gap' explains relapse, impulse buying, and why New Year's resolutions fail by February.

punchline.text: Calm you and emotional you are almost different people.

quiz.question: What is the 'empathy gap' in decision making?
options: Inability to predict how emotions change choices

details.summary: Decisions made in a hot emotional state, such as hunger, anger, or arousal, differ dramatically from those made in a cold, calm state. People consistently fail to predict how their preferences change when aroused.
details.whyItMatters: The hot-cold empathy gap explains why good intentions fail. People plan rationally in cool states but act on impulse when emotional intensity rises.
takeaways: Emotional state drastically changes preferences and choices
People cannot accurately predict their hot-state behavior
The empathy gap underlies failed resolutions and relapse

faq.question: What is a hot-cold empathy gap?
faq.answer: It is the inability to appreciate the power of visceral states when you are not currently experiencing them. When calm, you underestimate how hunger, anger, or pain will influence your future decisions. When aroused, you cannot imagine choosing differently. The gap works in both directions.

faq.question: How can you compensate for hot-cold empathy gaps?
faq.answer: Precommitment strategies work best. Set rules and remove temptations while in a cold state: do not keep junk food at home, set spending limits before shopping, make decisions about risky situations before they arise. Designing the environment beats relying on willpower in the moment.
